transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Raman (Redwood SE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Arielle Gomez (Peninsula Head of Security); Liam O'Connor (Eng Mgr); Fatima Noor (Cloud Arch); Noah Park (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Review of region controls and KMS. Questions on cross-border processing and sub-processors. Action: share SOC2 and KMS checklist, schedule deep technical workshop.

00:00 Marcus: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um I think folks have the calendar so we'll go ahead and kick off, this is Marcus from Redwood, with Priya and Diego on the call, super appreciate you taking the time today.
00:06 Arielle: thanks Marcus yeah appreciate it, we wanted to dig into specifics for EU residency and how you handle cross-border with sub-processors.
00:13 Priya: sure, um quick agenda — we'll cover architecture, KMS/HSM options, sub-processor map, logging/audit retention, and then open Q&A. sound good?
00:20 Liam: yep that's great.
00:28 Diego: just to set expectations if helpful — there are three deployment patterns we typically discuss: hosted (R-API), dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. Each has different controls for data locality and key management.
00:41 Arielle: can you explain region pinning more precisely? we need EU customer data to never leave the EU for processing, that's non-negotiable for regs.
00:48 Priya: absolutely yes. region pinning means we configure routing and tenancy so requests from EU tenants are pinned to EU regions, we maintain model variants and cached KV per region, and we enforce network egress rules so payloads don't cross out. that said there are edge cases — for fallbacks we can define policy like local-only fail or local-then-us with consent.
01:10 Fatima: what about backups or async processing — are those also geo-fenced?
01:16 Diego: good question. backups and long-term artifacts can be set to follow the same residency policy, we can optionally encrypt backups with a customer-managed key in EU KMS or a Bring-Your-Own-Key HSM.
01:29 Noah: legal question — who are your sub-processors in EU? we need a current inventory for our DPA review.
01:36 Marcus: we'll share the sub-processor list; currently we use a combination of cloud infra partners and a CDN in eu-central region, and for model hosting in eu-west we've got our dedicated hosters. we'll provide a CSV with versions and contract pointers.
01:50 Arielle: and SLA for data deletion if we terminate?
01:54 Marcus: standard contractual deletion within 30 days, can be contracted to 7 days for enterprise. we also provide confirmation of deletion and audit logs.
02:05 Liam: how do you keep keys? can we use our KMS? we can't have Redwood hold plain text keys for eu data.
02:11 Priya: yes we support customer-managed keys (CMK) — you can bring a key in your cloud provider KMS and we will encrypt model cache and at-rest artifacts with that key. for higher assurance we support HSM-backed keys and key escrow options for legal hold.
02:24 Fatima: so if we use our KMS, is any material transferred to the us in a way that would decrypt?
02:30 Diego: no. when you use CMK, Redwood never has the plaintext key. We call out that some control plane metadata may flow to control-plane endpoints in our control region for orchestration, but payloads remain encrypted and processing occurs in the pinned region. there's an architecture diagram we'll send that shows the control vs data plane split.
02:50 Arielle: careful, we've seen vendors conflate control-plane metadata and telemetry that can contain identifiers. we need audit logs that show exactly which tenant, which model, and which node processed requests, retained for 12 months.
03:03 Priya: we can produce tenant-scoped audit logs, with tokenized identifiers if you want pseudonymization; retention policies are configurable up to 24 months in the enterprise tier. logs include request traces, model version, latency, and node id but full request payloads are not retained unless you opt in for debugging.
03:22 Liam: payloads being optional is fine, but we need end-to-end encryption in transit and at rest. does Redwood support TLS mutual auth?
03:29 Marcus: yes mTLS supported for private deployments and recommended for Dedicated; hosted supports TLS 1.3 and customer-level segmentation via API keys and private networking.
03:40 Fatima: two quick pivot questions — 1) what about cross-border backups for disaster recovery? 2) are there subprocessors in the US that will see metadata?
03:49 Diego: for DR we can keep a secondary replica in another EU region; cross-border DR is optional and requires explicit agreement. Regarding subprocessors, some analytics and monitoring stacks are US-based; we can restrict telemetry export and provide on-prem collectors or EU-only partners for the enterprise package.
04:12 Arielle: hmm okay, how about encryption keys in transit to KMS — is the key exchange happening within eu?
04:18 Priya: yes if you provision your CMK in an EU region, all KMS calls stay within that region. Redwood uses signed requests to KMS and never exports raw key material.
04:26 Noah: about audits — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001? and are penetration test reports available under NDA?
04:33 Marcus: we have SOC 2 Type II and are ISO27001 certified; pen test reports can be provided under NDA. we'll drop those docs into your secure share after this call.
04:43 Arielle: can you also send a systemic diagram showing data flows for the EU tenant path?
04:48 Marcus: yes — action for Priya to annotate the network diagram with data plane flows.
04:53 05:01 Priya: let me talk about RBAC/SSO — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC SSO; role-based access controls allow tenant admins to restrict who can request keys or create model deployments. We also have fine-grained API token scopes.
05:21 Fatima: do you offer attribute-based access control? we have groups synced from our IdP and want that mirrored.
05:27 Priya: we support SCIM provisioning and group mapping, you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles; ABAC is on our roadmap, current pattern is role + group mapping.
05:37 Liam: latency — if we pin to EU, what's the expected p95 latency for short prompts? we are sensitive at 200ms.
05:44 Diego: typical p95 for small gen is 120–250ms depending on model family and sequence length; Dedicated pools in EU with pre-warmed kernels target <200ms p95. We can run a benchmark during the pilot against your typical payload.
06:05 Arielle: cost — dedicated or private will be more expensive, right?
06:09 Marcus: yes dedicated/private increases unit costs because of reserved GPU and isolated infra, but gives you stronger guarantees for residency and keys. we can show a cost model comparing hosted EU-only vs dedicated EU pool factoring in throughput.
06:24 Noah: subprocessors again — we need contractual flowdown. will Redwood put the sub-processor list into the DPA and give us a right to object?
06:33 Marcus: yes we include sub-processor list in the DPA and support objection processes for high risk subprocessors; we can also add flow-down clauses for security and audit.
06:42 Arielle: what about audit-level access? can we request logs in a consumable format for our auditors?
06:47 Priya: yes we can export logs in JSONL with fields aligned to your SIEM; we can also support real-time forwarder to your Splunk/Datadog instance inside EU.
06:58 Liam: do you maintain a sub-processor change log and notification window? we need 30 days notice for new subprocessors that process EU data.
07:06 Marcus: standard is 30 days notification for material sub-processor changes; for enterprise we can contractize it.
07:13 Fatima: hypothetical — what happens if an EU region is unavailable and you route to another region? we can't accept EU->US fallback.
07:21 Diego: you can configure fail-open vs fail-closed. Default best practice for residency-bound customers is fail-closed (requests fail if EU region not available) or fail-over to another EU region. We will not route to the US unless you approve explicit cross-border fallback.
07:38 Arielle: good. can you put that in the runbook?
07:41 Marcus: yes, runbook will list failover policy and exact error codes.
07:45 08:00 Priya: now KMS specifics — we have three patterns: provider-managed key, customer-managed key (CMK), and HSM-offered escrow. Provider-managed is simplest but not suitable for your case. CMK gives you key control; HSM escrow allows us to put a wrapped key in an HSM we both can attest to in case of legal hold.
08:21 Noah: HSM escrow — is that compliant with EU law enforcement requests? who responds to subpoenas?
08:28 Marcus: process-wise, subpoenas are handled by customers' cloud provider if keys are customer-managed; if provider-managed, Redwood must follow our legal team and DPA. We recommend CMK for maximum customer control.
08:41 Fatima: there's some tech detail we need — where is the KV cache stored, and is it encrypted with the same CMK?
08:47 Diego: KV cache (short term prompt cache) is stored in-memory on GPU instances and persisted to local encrypted object stores in the region; yes it can be encrypted with your CMK. long-term cache snapshots can be disabled.
08:59 Arielle: what's the retention for request logs and how are deletions handled?
09:04 Priya: request metadata is retained per your policy; deletion is a soft-then-hard delete — soft delete hides data immediately, hard delete purges within the contractual window and we provide certificate of deletion.
09:16 Liam: testing — we need to run a proof-of-concept to validate p95 and residency. What's realistic?
09:21 Marcus: typical pilot is 2–3 weeks: a VPC private deployment (or dedicated EU pool), run 10k requests/day with your sample payloads, we'll collect traces and provide a report.
09:33 Fatima: do you need our SOC2 to start a pilot?
09:36 Marcus: no, but it helps speed contract review; we can start an NDA and pilot agreement while finalizing DPA.
09:42 10:00 Arielle: small nit — in your docs you reference 'control plane home region' can you clarify what that means?
10:06 Priya: that's where orchestration and metadata live; it's logically separate from data plane. control plane may be in our global control region but we minimize PII in it; per your requirement we can request a control-plane EU option for enterprise installs.
10:21 Noah: will that add latency?
10:24 Diego: negligible for most requests since control-plane chatter is background; critical path remains data-plane processing in EU.
10:33 Liam: re: SSO and RBAC — we need audit events for admin actions (who created key, who changed routing). are those exposed?
10:41 Priya: yes admin audit events are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM with user attributes mapped to your IdP identity.
10:48 Arielle: what's the compliance posture for data subject requests? we need help fulfilling DSARs.
10:53 Marcus: we provide tooling that helps locate tenant data and orchestrate deletion/exports; for complex DSARs we'll collaborate with your team and provide logs and timelines.
11:02 Fatima: do you perform background checks on operator staff?
11:06 Marcus: yes we do role-based background checks for on-call and infra operators in enterprise settings, can share policy.
11:12 Arielle: okay, sounds good. quick question: any EU-based sub-processors doing model tuning with customer data?
11:18 Marcus: we do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly allowed in contract; model tuning partners are sandboxed and never ingest customer production data.
11:28 Diego: to add, we have a strict data usage policy in the DPA and technical guardrails to prevent production flows to training pipelines.
11:36 Liam: alright next — can you run through the deliverables you'll provide after this call?
11:40 Marcus: sure. 1) SOC2 Type II and ISO certs, 2) sub-processor inventory CSV, 3) control/data plane system diagram, 4) KMS onboarding checklist and HSM options, 5) pilot runbook template. we'll attach to CRM and upload to your secure share.
11:58 Priya: small note on telemetry — if you want no PII in telemetry we can mask identifiers at the edge and still preserve trace correlation ids.
12:06 Fatima: we want that masked by default.
12:09 Marcus: noted.
12:18 Arielle: any blockers on Redwood side for a 3-week EU pilot starting mid-Nov?
12:22 Marcus: team availability looks good; we just need the pilot scoping doc and your network peering details.
12:29 Diego: also need firewall rules and expected IP ranges, we'll supply an allowlist.
12:34 Noah: legal will follow up with DPA edits after we see sub-processor list.
12:38 Marcus: understood.
12:45 Arielle: okay let's recap.
12:48 Marcus: recap — Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and pen-test NDA docs, sub-processor inventory, system diagram, KMS checklist and HSM options. Peninsula to share tenant list, daily volumes, and network details. Schedule 2-hour infra deep dive. Pilot scoping to be finalized. Action items in the notes.
13:10 Liam: thanks all.
13:12 Arielle: thanks, we'll review and follow up.
13:15 Marcus: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with files and next steps.
13:20 [call ends]
